nodes.name: The spaces $L^2(0,T;\dbR)$, $L_\mathcal{F}^2(0,T;\dbR)$ and $C(0,T;\dbR)$
nodes.statement: \begin{eqnarray*} \begin{split} L^2(0,T;\dbR)=&\Big\{x:[0,T]\to \dbR\Bigm|x(\cdot)\ \text{\rm is deterministic such that}\int_0^T|x(s)|^2ds<\infty\Big\},\\ L_\mathcal{F}^2(0,T;\dbR)=&\Big\{x:[0,T]\times\Omega\to \dbR\Bigm| x(\cdot)\hbox{ is $\mathcal{F}_t$-adapted process such that } \dbE\int_0^T|x(s)|^2ds<\infty\Big\},\\ C(0,T;\dbR)=&\Big\{x:[0,T]\to \dbR\Bigm| x(\cdot)\hbox{ is deterministic and continuous on $[0,T]$} \Big\}. \end{split} \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: The three working spaces: deterministic square-integrable, $\mathcal{F}_t$-adapted square-integrable, and continuous deterministic functions on $[0,T]$.

nodes.name: mean field term (state average) $x^{N}$
nodes.statement: where $x^{N}=\frac{1}{N}\sum^{N}_{j=1}x_j$ is the mean field term which characterizes average interaction and mass effects of our population in \emph{spatial} variable
differentia: characterizes average interaction and mass effects of our population in \emph{spatial} variable

nodes.name: kernels $\varphi,b,c,\sigma$
nodes.statement: $\varphi,b,c,\sigma$ are deterministic functions, called the kernels, which characterize path dependence of out state in its \emph{temporal} variable
differentia: characterize path dependence of out state in its \emph{temporal} variable

nodes.name: resolvent kernel $P$
nodes.statement: where for any $0\leq t\leq s\leq T,$ \begin{eqnarray} P(s,t) =\sum\limits_{k=1}^{\infty }\Lambda^{k}(s,t), \quad \Lambda^{1}(s,t) =b(s,t), \quad \Lambda^{k+1}(s,t)=\int_{t}^{s}b(s,r)\Lambda^{k}(r,t)dr. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: The resolvent kernel $P$ is the sum of the iterated kernels $\Lambda^k$ generated by $b$.

nodes.name: modified control kernel $\widehat{c}$
nodes.statement: \begin{eqnarray} \widehat{c}(s,t)=c(s,t)+\int_{t}^{s}P(s,r)c(r,t)dr,\quad s\geq t. \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: transformed coefficients $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{\sigma}_i$, $\widehat{f}$
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \widehat{\varphi }(t) &=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}P(t,s)\varphi(s)ds, \nonumber\\ \widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t) &=\int_{0}^{t}\left[\sigma(t,s)+\int_{s}^{t}P(t,r)\sigma(r,s)dr\right] dW_{i}(s),\nonumber\\ \widehat{f}(t,s)&=f(t,s)+\int_{s}^{t}P(t,r)f(r,s)dr. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The resolvent-transformed initial, noise and coupling coefficients used to rewrite the state equation.

nodes.name: kernel $M(t,s)$
nodes.statement: \begin{eqnarray} M(t,s)=\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)dr,\quad t,s\in[0,T]. \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: the map $\Gamma a$
nodes.statement: Given $a(s)$, using Theorem \ref{theorem-1}, we can define $\Gamma a$ by \begin{equation} \lbrack \Gamma a](t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)a(s)ds +\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}M(t,s)\big\{\gamma a(s)+\eta-[\Gamma a](s)\big\}ds. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\Gamma$ maps a candidate mean-field trajectory $a$ to the expected optimal state it induces.

nodes.name: transformed coefficients $\widetilde{\varphi}$, $\widetilde{M}$
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \widetilde{\varphi}(t)&=\widehat{\varphi}(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widetilde{P}(t,s)\widehat{\varphi} (s)ds, \nonumber \\ \widetilde{M}(t,s)&=M(t,s)+\int_{0}^{t}\widetilde{P}(t,r)M(r,s)dr, \end{align}

nodes.name: second resolvent kernel $\widetilde{P}$
nodes.statement: \begin{eqnarray} \widetilde{P}(t,s) = \sum\limits_{k=1}^{\infty }\widetilde{\Lambda}^{k}(t,s), \quad \widetilde{\Lambda}^{1}(t,s) =\widehat{f}(t,s), \quad \widetilde{\Lambda}^{k+1}(t,s)=\int_{s}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,r)\widetilde{\Lambda}^{k}(r,s)dr. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: The resolvent kernel generated by $\widehat{f}$, used to remove the Volterra part of the NCE equation.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium
nodes.statement: Given a set of controls $\widehat{u}_i\in L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\dbR)$ with $i=1,2,\cdots,N$, if for any $i$, $1\leq i\leq N,$ $\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq \mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})+\epsilon, $ where $\epsilon>0$, $\widehat{u}_{-i}=(\widehat{u}_1,\cdots,\widehat{u}_{i-1},\widehat{u}_{i+1},\cdots,\widehat{u}_{N})$, $u_i\in L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\dbR)$, then we call this set of controls $\widehat{u}_i$, $1\leq i\leq N$ an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium with respect to costs $\mathcal{J}_i$ with $1\leq i\leq N$.
nodes.statement_short: Controls form an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium if no player can improve its cost by more than $\epsilon$ through a unilateral deviation.
nodes.genus: a set of controls $\widehat{u}_i\in L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\dbR)$ with $i=1,2,\cdots,N$

nodes.name: decentralized control $\widehat{u}_i$
nodes.statement: Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is the solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}), then we can define the decentralized control $\widehat{u}_i$ for agent $\mathcal{A}_i$ as follows: \begin{equation} \widehat{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(s,t)[x_{i}(s)-\gamma \widehat{a}(s)-\eta]ds \end{equation} where $x_i$ is the solution of (\ref{2.1}) corresponding to $\widehat{u}_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Each agent's decentralized strategy is a conditional-expectation feedback of its own future state against the NCE trajectory $\widehat{a}$.

nodes.name: stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation
nodes.statement: Secondly, equation (\ref{3.9}) is a new type of stochastic equation with double integrals, which is essentially different from the corresponding equation in stochastic differential equations (SDEs) case. Since it has both the characters of Volterra and Fredholm equation, we then call it a stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation.
nodes.statement_short: An equation with double integrals combining Volterra and Fredholm structure, satisfied by the optimal state.
nodes.genus: a new type of stochastic equation with double integrals
differentia: it has both the characters of Volterra and Fredholm equation

nodes.name: transformed kernel $\widehat{B}$ and resolvent $P_0$
nodes.statement: Here we denote by \begin{eqnarray} &&\widehat{B}(t,r)=B(t,r)+\int_{r}^{t}P_0(t,v)B(v,r)dv,\quad t,v\in[0,T],\nonumber\\ &&P_0(t,v) =\sum\limits_{k=1}^{\infty}\Lambda^{k}(t,v), \quad \Lambda^{1}(t,t) =A(t,v), \quad \Lambda^{k+1}(t,v)=\int_{v}^{t}A(t,r)\Lambda^{k}(r,v)dr . \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: The abstract analogues of $\widehat{c}$ and $P$ for generic kernels $A$, $B$ in the solvability lemma.

nodes.name: perturbation magnitudes $\epsilon_a$, $\epsilon_b$
nodes.statement: In the following part, given two processes $\xi _{a}$, $\xi _{b}$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\dbR)$, we denote by \begin{eqnarray} \epsilon _{a}=\left( \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\xi _{a}(t)|^{2}dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}<\infty , \quad \epsilon _{b}=\left( \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}<\infty . \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: fundamental solution $\Phi_1$ for the state-delay system
nodes.statement: By introducing function $\Phi_1 $ as \begin{eqnarray} \left\{\begin{array}{rl} \dsp\frac{\partial \Phi_1(t,s)}{\partial t} & = \dsp A(t)\Phi_1(t-h,s)+\int_{t-h}^{t}B(t,r)\Phi_1(r,s)dr,\ t\geq 0, \\ [5mm] \Phi_1(0,0) & = 1, \quad \Phi_1(t,s)=0, \quad t<0, \end{array}\right. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_1$ solves the delay differential equation attached to the state-delay dynamics and acts as its fundamental solution.
nodes.section: 4.2 SDEs with delay in the state process

nodes.name: fundamental solution $\Phi_2$ for the control-delay system
nodes.statement: Similarly, by introducing function $\Phi_2 $ as \begin{eqnarray} \frac{\partial \Phi_2(t,s)}{\partial t} =A(t)\Phi_2(t,s) \quad \Phi_2(s,s) =1,\quad t,s\in[0,T], \end{eqnarray}
nodes.section: 4.3 SDEs with delay in the control

nodes.name: one-dimensional state equation
nodes.statement: In this paper, we set the state equation to be one-dimensional for sake of notation simplicity. There has no essential difficulty to extend the results to the multi-dimensional case.

nodes.name: complete filtered probability space and independent Brownian motions
nodes.statement: Suppose $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, (\mathcal{F}_t)_{0\leq t\leq T}, \mathbb{P})$ is a complete filtered probability space on which $W(t)=(W_i(t))_{0 \leq t \leq T}$, $1\leq i\leq N$ are independent scalar-valued Brownian motions. It is also assumed $(\mathcal F_t)_{0\leq t\leq T}$ is the natural filtration generated by $W(t)$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_T$.

nodes.name: smallness condition (6.2) on the kernels $\widehat{B}$, $B$
nodes.statement: \begin{eqnarray} T\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}|\widehat{B}(t,r)B(s,r)|^{2}drdsdt<\frac{R^{2}}{3}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: A smallness condition on the double-integral kernel relative to the control weight $R$.

nodes.name: $f=0$ in the special cases
nodes.statement: For sake of simplicity, we suppose $f=0$ in the following.

nodes.name: linear stochastic differential equation for individual state in standard mean-field LQG games
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} dx_i(t)=\big[A_i x_i(t)+B_i u_i(t)+F_i x^{(N)}(t)\big]dt+D_idW_{i}(t), \end{equation}
nodes.origin_citation: Huang, Malhame & Caines 2006; Lasry & Lions 2007; Nguyen & Huang 2012

nodes.name: cost functional of the standard mean-field LQG game
nodes.statement: The cost functional to be minimized takes the following form: \begin{eqnarray*} J_{i}(u_i(\cdot)) = \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left\{\int_0^{T}\Big[Q(x_i(t)-x^{(N)}(t))^2 +Ru^2_i(t)\Big]dt+Hx_i^{2}(T)\right\}. \end{eqnarray*}

nodes.name: controlled stochastic Volterra integral equation (state dynamics of $\mathcal{A}_i$)
nodes.statement: \begin{eqnarray} x_{i}(t) & = & \varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds\nonumber\\ & & +\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s). \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: The state of agent $\mathcal{A}_i$ solves a controlled stochastic Volterra integral equation coupled to the population average $x^{N}$.

nodes.name: differential (time-independent kernel) special case of the state equation
nodes.statement: The first one is the differential case, i.e., the kernels $\varphi,b,c,\sigma $ are independent of $t.$ In this case, equation (\ref{2.1}) becomes the following stochastic \emph{integral} equation, \begin{eqnarray} x_{i}(t)=x(0)+\int_{0}^{t}b(s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(s)dW_i(s). \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: stochastic differential equation with delay in the state
nodes.statement: The second case is the stochastic differential equation with delay in state which can be described as \begin{equation} dx_{i}(t)=\left[ A(t)x_{i}(t-h)+\int_{t-h}^{t}B(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds\right] dt+C(t)u_i(t)dt+D(t)dW_i(t), \end{equation} where $h>0$ is the delay or lag parameter, $x_{i}(t)=k(t),$ $t\in \lbrack -h,0].$

nodes.name: stochastic differential equation with delay in the control
nodes.statement: The third one includes stochastic differential equations with delay in control variable which evolves as \begin{equation} dx_{i}(t)=A(t)x_{i}(t)dt+C(t)u_i(t-h)dt+D(t)dW_i(t), \end{equation} where $h>0,$ $x_{i}(t)=k(t),$ $t\in \lbrack -h,0].$

nodes.name: optimal control $\overline{u}_i$ of the limiting problem via BSVIE adjoint
nodes.statement: In this case, it follows from \cite{S-W-Y 2013} or \cite{Y 2008} that the optimal control $\overline{u}_{i}$ can be represented by \begin{equation} \overline{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{2R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}c(s,t) \overline{y}_{i}(s)ds \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The optimal control is a conditional expectation of the BSVIE adjoint process weighted by the control kernel.

nodes.name: linear Backward Stochastic Volterra Integral Equation (BSVIE) for $\overline{y}_i$
nodes.statement: where $\overline{y}_i$ satisfies the following linear Backward Stochastic Volterra Integral Equation (BSVIE) \begin{equation} \overline{y}_{i}(t)=2\overline{x}_{i}(t)-2\gamma a(t)-2\eta +\int_{t}^{T}b(s,t)\overline{y}_{i}(s)ds-\int_{t}^{T}\overline{z}_{i}(t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{equation} and $\overline{x}_{i}$ is the solution of (\ref{3.1}) with respect to $\overline{u}_i$.

nodes.name: resolvent representation of the adjoint $\overline{y}_i$
nodes.statement: Due to the special form of (\ref{3.4}), by using Lemma 1.1 in \cite{Y 1996} we can formulate $\overline{y}_{i}$ as \begin{equation} \overline{y}_{i}(t)=2\overline{x}_{i}(t)-2\gamma a(t)-2\eta +\int_{t}^{T}2P(s,t)[\overline{x}_{i}(s)-\gamma a(s)-\eta ]ds, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A variation-of-constants formula expressing the adjoint explicitly through the resolvent kernel $P$.

nodes.name: optimal control in resolvent form
nodes.statement: Substituting (\ref{3.5}) into (\ref{3.3}), we can rewrite the optimal control in (\ref{3.3}) as \begin{equation} \overline{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(s,t)[\overline{x}_{i}(s)-\gamma a(s)-\eta ]ds, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The optimal control expressed directly in the state through the modified kernel $\widehat{c}$.

nodes.name: resolvent form of the limiting state equation
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by using Lemma 1.1. of \cite{Y 1996}, we can rewrite (\ref{3.1}) as \begin{equation} x_{i}(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)+\widehat{\sigma }_i(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)a(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The state equation rewritten without the Volterra drift term, using the transformed coefficients.

nodes.name: optimal state equation of the limiting control problem (stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation)
nodes.statement: Consequently, by combining (\ref{3.6}) and (\ref{3.8}), as well as stochastic Fubini theorem, the optimal state equation of this limit control problem can be described by \begin{align} \overline{x}_{i}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\widehat{\sigma}_i (t)-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}\overline{x}_{i}(s)drds \nonumber\\ & + \int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)a(s)ds+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t} \widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)dr\cdot[\gamma a(s)+\eta ]ds. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The closed-loop optimal state solves a stochastic equation with double integrals of Volterra-Fredholm type.

nodes.name: Fredholm integral equation for $\dbE\overline{x}_i$
nodes.statement: In particular, by taking expectation, \begin{equation} \dbE\overline{x}_{i}(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)a(s)ds+\frac{1}{R} \int_{0}^{T}M(t,s)[\gamma a(s)+\eta-\dbE\overline{x}_{i}(s)]ds, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Taking expectations turns the optimal state equation into a deterministic Fredholm equation with kernel $M$.

nodes.name: Nash certainty equivalence (NCE) equation
nodes.statement: The Nash certainty equivalence (NCE) equation in our setting is thus \begin{equation} \widehat{a}(t)=\widehat{\varphi}(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s) \widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}M(t,s)[(\gamma-1)\widehat{a}(s)+\eta ]ds, \end{equation} where $\widehat{a}$ is the corresponding solution. Note that (\ref{3.14}) is a linear deterministic Volterra-Fredholm integral equation.
nodes.statement_short: The consistency condition: the frozen mean field $\widehat{a}$ must reproduce itself, giving a linear deterministic Volterra-Fredholm equation.

nodes.name: NCE equation in pure Fredholm form
nodes.statement: More precisely, by using Lemma 1.1. in \cite{Y 1996}, we can rewrite (\ref{3.14}) as \begin{equation} \widehat{a}(t)=\widetilde{\varphi}(t)+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\widetilde{M}(t,s)[(\gamma -1)\widehat{a}(s)+\eta ]ds, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The Volterra part of the NCE equation is absorbed by the resolvent $\widetilde{P}$, leaving a Fredholm equation.

nodes.name: closed-loop state equation under the decentralized controls
nodes.statement: Substituting (\ref{3.18}) into equation (\ref{2.1}), together with the transformation in (\ref{3.8}), we get \begin{align} x_{i}(t)=& \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\widehat{\sigma }_i(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds\nonumber\\ &- \int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{s}}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta]drds, \end{align} where $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{\sigma}_i$ and $\widehat{f}$ are defined in (\ref{3.8.1}).
nodes.statement_short: The realized $N$-player state dynamics when every agent applies its decentralized control.

nodes.name: limiting optimal state with $a=\widehat{a}$
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by replacing $a$ by $\widehat{a}$ in (\ref{3.9}), we get \begin{align} \overline{x}_{i}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\widehat{\sigma_i} (t)-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c} (s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}\overline{x}_{i}(s)drds \nonumber \\ & +\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t} \widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)dr\cdot \lbrack \gamma \widehat{a}(s)+\eta ]ds. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The limiting optimal state trajectory obtained by freezing the mean field at the NCE solution.

nodes.name: state dynamics when all players except $\mathcal{A}_i$ use $\widehat{u}_j$
nodes.statement:
If we apply control $\widehat{u}_j$ in (ef{3.18}) to all the player except $\mathcal{A}_i,$ that is, for $j
eq i$,  egin{align} x_{j}(t) = & \; \varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{j}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds 
onumber \ & +\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\widehat{u}_{j}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{j}(s), \end{align} while for player $i$,  egin{align} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds 
onumber \ &+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s)+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds, \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The perturbed system in which agent $i$ deviates to an arbitrary $u_i$ while all others keep their decentralized controls.

nodes.name: mean field LQG game for the stochastic integral system: individual cost functional $\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,u_{-i})$
nodes.statement: All individual players are coupled in terms of their individual cost functional as follows: \begin{equation} \mathcal{J}_{i}(u_{i},u_{-i})=\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left[ (x_{i}(t)-\gamma x^{N}(t)-\eta )^{2}+Ru_{i}^{2}(t)\right] dt, \end{equation} where $u_{-i}=(u_1,\cdots,u_{i-1},u_{i+1},\cdots,u_{N})$, and $R>0$, $\gamma$, $\eta$ are constants.
nodes.statement_short: Each of the $N$ agents minimizes a quadratic cost that penalizes deviation of its state from a $\gamma$-scaled population average.

nodes.name: auxiliary limiting control problem
nodes.statement: First, let us formulate one auxiliary limiting control problem via the approximation of state average $x^{N}$ by some deterministic function $a(t)$. Now we introduce the following state equation \begin{eqnarray} x_{i}(t)&=&\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)a(s)ds\nonumber \\ &&+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s),\quad t\in[0,T], \end{eqnarray} and the cost functional for player $\mathcal{A}_i$ ($i=1,2,\cdots,N$), \begin{eqnarray} \overline{J}_{i}(u_{i})=\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\Big[(x_{i}(t)-\gamma a(t)-\eta )^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\Big] dt. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: A single-agent LQ problem obtained by replacing the population average with a frozen deterministic function $a(t)$.

nodes.name: perturbed limiting control problem with $\xi_a$, $\xi_b$
nodes.statement: First let us recall the optimal control problem of which optimal control $\overline{u}_{i}$ and optimal state equation $\overline{x}_{i}$ are given by (\ref{3.6}) and (\ref{3.9}) with $a=\widehat{a}.$ For comparison, we also discuss one perturbed version with state equation \begin{align} x_{i}(t) = & \;\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\ &+\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align} and the cost functional \[ J_{i}^{\xi }(u_{i})=\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left[ |x_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta +\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\right]dt. \] Here $g$ is bounded deterministic function.
nodes.statement_short: The limiting problem with additive state and cost perturbations $\xi_a$, $\xi_b$, used for the $\epsilon$-Nash estimate.

nodes.name: explicit resolvent kernel and coefficients in the SDE case
nodes.statement: For $s,t\in[0,T],$ we have \[ \Lambda^{1}(s,t)=b(t), \quad \Lambda^{k+1}(s,t)=b(t)\left(\int_{t}^{s}b(r)dr\right)^{k}, \quad P(s,t)=b(t)e^{\int_{t}^{s}b(u)du}. \] Therefore, \begin{eqnarray*} & & \widehat{\varphi }(t) = x(0)e^{\int_{0}^{t}b(r)dr}, \quad \widehat{\sigma}_i(t) =\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (s)e^{\int_{s}^{t}b(r)dr}dW_{i}(s), \\ & & \widehat{c}(s,t)=c(t)e^{\int_{t}^{s}b(r)dr}, \quad M(t,s)=\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}|c(r)|^{2}e^{\int_{r}^{t}b(v)dv+\int_{r}^{s}b(v)dv}dr. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: In the SDE case the resolvent kernel and all transformed coefficients reduce to explicit exponentials of $\int b$.
nodes.section: 4.1 The case of stochastic differential equation

nodes.name: NCE equation in the SDE case
nodes.statement: The NCE equation in this setting takes the following rather simple form \begin{eqnarray} \widehat{a}(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}|c(r)|^{2}e^{\int_{r}^{t}b(v)dv+\int_{r}^{s}b(v)dv}dr\cdot\big\{\gamma \widehat{a}(s)+\eta-\widehat{a}(s)\big\}ds. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.section: 4.1 The case of stochastic differential equation

nodes.name: decentralized control and closed-loop state in the SDE case
nodes.statement: We define by \begin{eqnarray} \widehat{u}_i(t)=-\frac{1}{R}c(t)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_t}\!\!\int_t^Te^{\int_t^sb(r)dr}[x_i(s) -\gamma\widehat{a}(s)-\eta]ds,\quad 1\leq i\leq N, \end{eqnarray} where $\widehat{a}$ is the solution of NCE equation and \begin{align} x_{i}(t) = & \; x(0)e^{\int_{0}^{t}b(r)dr}+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (s)e^{\int_{s}^{t}b(r)dr}dW_{i}(s) \nonumber \\ & -\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}|c(s)|^2\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{s}}\int_{s}^{T}e^{\int_{s}^{r}b(v)dv+\int_s^tb(r)dr} [x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta]drds, \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The decentralized strategy and the resulting state in the SDE special case, written with exponential kernels.
nodes.section: 4.1 The case of stochastic differential equation

nodes.name: Volterra reformulation of the state-delay SDE
nodes.statement: we transform (\ref{4.5}) into (see \cite{L 1973}, \cite{O-Z 2010}) \begin{eqnarray} x_{i}(t)=\psi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}K(t,s)u_i(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\Phi_1 (t,s)D(s)dW_i(s), \end{eqnarray} where $K(t,s)=\Phi_1(t,s)C(s),$ and \begin{eqnarray*} \psi(t)=\Phi_1(t,0)k(0)+\int_{-h}^{0}\left[ \Phi_1 (t,s+h)A(s+h)+\int_{0}^{h}\Phi_1(t,u)B(u,s)du\right] k(s)ds . \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: The state-delay SDE is recast as a stochastic Volterra integral equation using the fundamental solution $\Phi_1$.
nodes.section: 4.2 SDEs with delay in the state process

nodes.name: specialized kernels for the state-delay case
nodes.statement: On the other hand, (\ref{4.7}) is one special case of Equation (\ref{2.1}) by letting $b=0,$ hence for $t,s\in[0,T]$, \begin{eqnarray*} & & P(t,s) = 0, \quad \widehat{c}(s,t)=\Phi_1(t,s)C(s), \\ & & \widehat{\varphi }(t) = \psi(t), \quad \widehat{\sigma}_{i}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}\Phi_1(t,s)D(s)dW_{i}(s),\\ & & M(t,s) = \int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\Phi_1(t,r)\Phi_1(s,r)|C(r)|^{2}dr. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: With $b=0$ the resolvent vanishes and all transformed coefficients are given directly by $\Phi_1$.
nodes.section: 4.2 SDEs with delay in the state process

nodes.name: NCE equation for the state-delay case
nodes.statement: The NCE equation in this situation becomes \begin{eqnarray} \widehat{a}(t)=\psi(t)+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\Phi_1(t,r)\Phi(s,r)|C(r)|^{2}dr\cdot\big\{\gamma \widehat{a}(s)+\eta-\widehat{a}(s)\big\}ds. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.section: 4.2 SDEs with delay in the state process

nodes.name: decentralized control and state for the state-delay case
nodes.statement: Given $\widehat{a}$ being a solution of NCE equation, if we define \begin{eqnarray} \widehat{u}_i(t)=-\frac 1 R C(t)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_t}\int_t^T\Phi_1(s,t) [x_i(s) -\gamma \widehat{a}(s)-\eta]ds,\quad 1\leq i\leq N, \end{eqnarray} where \begin{align*} x_{i}(t) = & \; \psi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\Phi_1(t,s)D(s)dW_{i}(s) \\ & -R^{-1}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\Phi_1(t,r)\Phi_1(s,r)|C(r)|^{2}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}[x_{i}(s)-\gamma \widehat{a}(s)-\eta]drds, \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The decentralized strategy and closed-loop state for state-delayed dynamics, expressed through $\Phi_1$.
nodes.section: 4.2 SDEs with delay in the state process

nodes.name: Volterra reformulation of the control-delay SDE
nodes.statement: we can transform equation (\ref{4.10}) into \begin{eqnarray} x_{i}(t)=\psi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}K(t,s)u_i(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\Phi_2(t,s)D(s)dW_i(s), \end{eqnarray} where \[ \psi(t)=\Phi_2(t,0)k(0), \quad K(t,s)=\Phi_2(t,s+h)C(s+h), \quad t,s\in[0,T]. \]
nodes.statement_short: The control-delay SDE becomes a stochastic Volterra equation whose control kernel is shifted by the lag $h$.
nodes.section: 4.3 SDEs with delay in the control

nodes.name: specialized kernels for the control-delay case
nodes.statement: Therefore, (\ref{4.12}) is one special case of (\ref{2.1}) with $b=0,$ and \begin{eqnarray*} & & P(t,s) = 0,\quad \widehat{c}(s,t)=\Phi_2(s,t+h)C(t+h), \\ & & \widehat{\varphi }(t) = \Phi_2(t,0)k(0),\quad \widehat{\sigma }_i(t)=\int_{0}^{t}\Phi_2(t,s)D(s)dW_{i}(s),\\ & & M(t,s) = \int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\Phi_2(t,r+h)\Phi_2(s,r+h)|C(r+h)|^{2}dr. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: With $b=0$ all transformed coefficients are given by the lag-shifted fundamental solution $\Phi_2$.
nodes.section: 4.3 SDEs with delay in the control

nodes.name: NCE equation for the control-delay case
nodes.statement: The NCE equation in this situation becomes \begin{equation} \widehat{a}(t)=\psi (t)+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\Phi_2(t,r+h)\Phi_2(s,r+h)|C(r+h)|^{2}dr \cdot \big\{\gamma\widehat{a}(s)+\eta-\widehat{a}(s)\big\}ds. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4.3 SDEs with delay in the control

nodes.name: decentralized control and state for the control-delay case
nodes.statement: Given $\widehat{a}$ being the NCE solution, we define \begin{eqnarray} \widehat{u}_{i}(t)=-\frac{1}{R}C(t+h)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\3n\int_{t}^{T}\Phi_2 (s,t+h)[x_{i}(s)-\gamma \widehat{a}(s)-\eta]ds,\quad t\in[0,T], \end{eqnarray} while $x_{i}$ satisfies \begin{align*} x_{i}(t) = & \; \Phi_2(t,0)k(0)+\int_{0}^{t}\Phi_2(t,s)D(s)dW_{i}(s) \\ & -R^{-1}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}\Phi_2(t,r+h)\Phi_2(s,r+h)|C(r+h)|^{2}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}[x_{i}(s)-\gamma\widehat{a}(s)-\eta]drds, \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The decentralized strategy and closed-loop state for control-delayed dynamics, expressed through $\Phi_2$.
nodes.section: 4.3 SDEs with delay in the control

nodes.name: Remark 3.1 (resolvent kernel $P$ is bounded and continuous)
nodes.statement: Note that (\ref{3.5}) can be viewed as a constant variation formula in our setup and $P$ is called ``resolvent kernel". In the special multi-dimensional differential case, $P$ becomes the solution of fundamental matrix. The method of infinite series will be frequently adopted in our following analysis. On the other hand, it is straightforward to verify \[ |\Lambda^{k}(s,t)|<\frac{M^{k}|t-s|^{k-1}}{(k-1)!},\quad t,s\in[0,T],\quad k\geq 1, \] where $M$ is the upper bound of $b$, thus $P$ is bounded. Moreover, if $b$ is continuous in $t,$ then one can see that $P$ is also continuous in $t.$
nodes.statement_short: The factorial decay of the iterated kernels makes the resolvent series converge, so $P$ is bounded and inherits continuity from $b$.

nodes.name: Remark 3.2 (on the role and generality of equation (6.1))
nodes.statement: Some comment to (\ref{6.1}). To be shown later, it plays some key role in our remaining analysis. Since our first concern here is the solvability of (\ref{6.1}) under certain conditions. In such sense, we do not pursue the most general assumptions here and we hope to weaken these conditions in our future work.

nodes.name: Remark 3.3 (generality of Lemma 3.7 and its technical conditions)
nodes.statement: Compared with Lemma 3.4 above, our result here seems to be more general because $u_i$ in (\ref{6.13}) is not necessary to be $\widehat{u}_i$ in (\ref{3.18}). Moreover, our result also generalizes the corresponding result in \cite{N-H 2012} in that our state equation can degenerate to the linear SDEs there. In addition, our approach here is also different from the one used in \cite{N-H 2012}. At last, although the conditions imposed on above coefficients $K_1$, $K_2$ and $L$ seem to be technical, it has two interesting features. First, the above inequality holds true in general because $N$ is always sufficiently large. Second, such condition is not required in the nontrivial case $\widehat{f}=0.$
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.7 generalizes both Lemma 3.4 and the SDE result of Nguyen & Huang, and its technical condition is harmless for large $N$.

nodes.name: Remark 4.1 (Riccati representation of $\widehat{u}_i$ in the SDE case)
nodes.statement: One can express $\widehat{u}_i$ in (\ref{4.3}) as $\widehat{u}_i(t)=\frac 1 R c(t)[-P'(t)x_i(t)+\delta(t)]$ where $P'$ and $\delta$ satisfy Riccati equation and backward ordinary differential equation respectively, see for example, \cite{H 2010}, \cite{H-C-M 2007} and \cite{N-H 2012}. Such procedure is different from ours here. More precise, it makes use the advantage of state equation and optimal control (note that $s$ and $t$ are separable). However, such skills are hard to be applied in more general model such as the state equations with delay below. In such sense, our approach applied here is more flexiable which can fill this technical gap.
nodes.statement_short: In the separable SDE case the control admits the classical Riccati feedback form, but that route fails for delayed/Volterra models.
nodes.section: 4.1 The case of stochastic differential equation

nodes.name: generic constant convention
nodes.statement: In the following, we denote by $C$ a generic positive constant independent of $N$ that may change from line to line.

nodes.name: path dependence and non-separability of $\widehat{c}$
nodes.statement: Firstly, note that $\overline{u}_i(t)$ depends on the path of $\overline{x}_i$ in $[t,T]$. Moreover, $\widehat{c}$ is a general non-separable function of $(t,s)$. In particular, such a general feature can naturally degenerate and transform into the form with Riccati equation involved, see Section 4.1 below.
nodes.statement_short: The optimal control is genuinely path dependent because $\widehat{c}$ is non-separable, unlike the Riccati case.

nodes.name: Volterra kernel in the cost functional and time-inconsistent LQG games
nodes.statement: On one hand, it is possible to include the Volterra integral kernel into the cost functional to be minimized. This provides some potential way to study the LQG game with time inconsistency.

nodes.name: delay-dependent consistency conditions for mean-field games
nodes.statement: On the other hand, this paper also considers the mean-field games with stochastic delayed system. Actually, more extensive research can be given in this research line and it is anticipated some new consistency conditions can be given which depend on the delay characters.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1 (solvability of the Fredholm integral equation)
nodes.statement: Consider the following Fredholm integral equation \begin{equation} x(t)=\psi (t)+\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}A(t,s)x(s)ds,\quad t\in[0,T], \end{equation} where $\psi $, $A$ are bounded and continuous functions in $t$. If \[ \sup_{t\in [0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}|A(t,s)|^{2}ds<R, \quad \sup_{t\in [0,T]}|\psi (t)|^{2}<\infty , \] then there exists a unique continuous solution $x(\cdot)$ of (\ref{3.12}).
nodes.statement_short: A Fredholm equation with a kernel small relative to $R$ has a unique continuous solution.
assumptions: where $\psi $, $A$ are bounded and continuous functions in $t$
$\sup_{t\in [0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}|A(t,s)|^{2}ds<R, \quad \sup_{t\in [0,T]}|\psi (t)|^{2}<\infty ,$
conclusions: there exists a unique continuous solution $x(\cdot)$ of (\ref{3.12})

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1 (unique solvability of the expected optimal state equation)
nodes.statement: Suppose $\varphi,$ $b$, $f$, $c$ are bounded and continuous in $t$ such that \[ \sup_{t\in \lbrack 0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}|M(t,s)|^{2}ds<R. \] Then, given $a\in C[0,T]$, there exists a unique continuous function $\dbE \overline{x}_i(\cdot)$ satisfying equation (\ref{3.10}).
nodes.statement_short: Under a smallness condition on $M$, the Fredholm equation for the expected optimal state has a unique continuous solution.
assumptions: Suppose $\varphi,$ $b$, $f$, $c$ are bounded and continuous in $t$ such that $\sup_{t\in \lbrack 0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}|M(t,s)|^{2}ds<R.$
given $a\in C[0,T]$
conclusions: there exists a unique continuous function $\dbE \overline{x}_i(\cdot)$ satisfying equation (\ref{3.10})

nodes.name: Theorem 3.2 (unique solvability of the NCE equation)
nodes.statement: Suppose $\varphi,b,c,f$ are bounded and continuous in $t.$ If \[ \sup_{t\in [0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert (\gamma-1)\widetilde{M}(t,s)\right\vert ^{2}ds<R, \] then (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique solution $a \in C[0,T]$.
nodes.statement_short: A smallness condition on $(\gamma-1)\widetilde{M}$ gives a unique continuous solution of the NCE equation.
assumptions: Suppose $\varphi,b,c,f$ are bounded and continuous in $t.$
$\sup_{t\in [0,T]}\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert (\gamma-1)\widetilde{M}(t,s)\right\vert ^{2}ds<R,$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.2 (well-posedness and a priori estimate for equation (6.1))
nodes.statement: Suppose \begin{eqnarray} x(t)=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}A(t,s)x(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}B(t,r)B(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}x(s)drds, \end{eqnarray} where $\varphi (\cdot )\in L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\dbR),$ $A,B$ are deterministic and bounded functions such that \begin{eqnarray} T\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}|\widehat{B}(t,r)B(s,r)|^{2}drdsdt<\frac{R^{2}}{3}. \end{eqnarray} Here we denote by \begin{eqnarray} &&\widehat{B}(t,r)=B(t,r)+\int_{r}^{t}P_0(t,v)B(v,r)dv,\quad t,v\in[0,T],\nonumber\\ &&P_0(t,v) =\sum\limits_{k=1}^{\infty}\Lambda^{k}(t,v), \quad \Lambda^{1}(t,t) =A(t,v), \quad \Lambda^{k+1}(t,v)=\int_{v}^{t}A(t,r)\Lambda^{k}(r,v)dr . \end{eqnarray} Then (\ref{6.1}) admits a unique solution $x(\cdot)\in L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\dbR)$ satisfying \begin{eqnarray} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x(s)|^{2}ds\leq 6\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi}(s)|^{2}ds, \end{eqnarray} where \begin{eqnarray*} \widehat{\varphi }(t) &=&\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}P_0(t,s)\varphi (s)ds,\quad t\in[0,T]. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: The abstract stochastic Volterra-Fredholm equation is uniquely solvable in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}$ with the $L^2$ bound $6\dbE\int|\widehat{\varphi}|^2$.
assumptions: $\varphi (\cdot )\in L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\dbR),$ $A,B$ are deterministic and bounded functions
$T\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}|\widehat{B}(t,r)B(s,r)|^{2}drdsdt<\frac{R^{2}}{3}.$
conclusions: (\ref{6.1}) admits a unique solution $x(\cdot)\in L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\dbR)$ satisfying $\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x(s)|^{2}ds\leq 6\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi}(s)|^{2}ds,$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.3 ($O(1/N)$ closeness of $\widehat{a}$ and the limiting state average)
nodes.statement: Suppose NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique solution $\widehat{a}(\cdot)$, and (\ref{6.2}), (\ref{6.3}) hold with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$, then \begin{eqnarray} \dbE\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-\overline{x}^{N}(s)|^2ds=O\Big(\frac{1}{N}\Big), \end{eqnarray} where $\overline{x}^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{i=1}^{N}\overline{x}_{i}(t)$ and $\overline{x}_i$ satisfies (\ref{3.20}).
nodes.statement_short: The average of the limiting optimal states converges to the NCE solution at rate $O(1/N)$ in $L^2$.
assumptions: Suppose NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique solution $\widehat{a}(\cdot)$
(\ref{6.2}), (\ref{6.3}) hold with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.4 ($O(1/N)$ closeness of the true and limiting states)
nodes.statement: Suppose NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a solution $\widehat{a}$, (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c},$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$, then \begin{eqnarray} \dbE\int_0^T|\widehat{a}(s)-x^{N}(s)|^2ds+\sup\limits_{1\leq i\leq N}\dbE\int_0^T|x_i(t)-\overline{x}_i(t)|^2dt=O\Big(\frac 1 N\Big) \end{eqnarray} where $x^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{i=1}^{N}x_{i}(t),$ $x_i$ satisfies (\ref{3.19}).
nodes.statement_short: Both the realized state average and each individual state are within $O(1/N)$ of their mean-field limits.
assumptions: Suppose NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a solution $\widehat{a}$
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c},$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$

nodes.name: Theorem 3.3 (cost approximation of order $O(1/\sqrt{N})$)
nodes.statement: Suppose $\varphi$, $f$, $b$ and $c$ are bounded and continuous in $t$, NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique continuous solution $\widehat{a}\in C[0,T]$, $\overline{u}_i$ is the optimal control with state equation (\ref{3.1}), cost functional (\ref{3.2}) that is parameterized by $\widehat{a}$, (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c},$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Then for $1\leq i\leq N$, we have \begin{eqnarray} \mid\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-\overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)\mid=O\left(\frac {1} {\sqrt{N}}\right). \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: The realized cost under the decentralized controls differs from the limiting optimal cost by $O(1/\sqrt{N})$.

NCE equation (\ref{3.14}) admits a unique continuous solution $\widehat{a}\in C[0,T]$
$\overline{u}_i$ is the optimal control with state equation (\ref{3.1}), cost functional (\ref{3.2}) that is parameterized by $\widehat{a}$
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c},$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.5 (near-optimality of $\overline{u}_i$ under perturbation)
nodes.statement: Suppose $\overline{u}_{i}$ is an optimal control given in (\ref{3.6}) and \begin{eqnarray} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt+\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C_{0}. \end{eqnarray} where $ x_{i},$ $u_{i}$ are defined in (\ref{6.7}), $C_{0}$ is a fixed constant. Moreover, $\widehat{a}$ is continuous and bounded, (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c},$ then we have \[ J_{i}^{\xi }(u_{i})\geq \overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i})-C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b). \]
nodes.statement_short: The perturbed cost cannot fall below the unperturbed optimal cost by more than $C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b)$.
assumptions: Suppose $\overline{u}_{i}$ is an optimal control given in (\ref{3.6})
$\widehat{a}$ is continuous and bounded, (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c},$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.6 (boundedness of $\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$)
nodes.statement: Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}), (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, and $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$. Then $\mathcal{J}_{i}(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq C$, where $C$ does not depend on $N$.
nodes.statement_short: The realized cost under the decentralized controls is bounded uniformly in $N$.
assumptions: Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14})
(\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, and $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$
conclusions: $\mathcal{J}_{i}(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq C$, where $C$ does not depend on $N$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.7 ($O(1/N)$ closeness under a unilateral deviation)
nodes.statement: Suppose $\widehat{a}$ is the solution of NCE equation (\ref{3.14}), (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for two cases of $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$ and $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Moreover, $(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2<\frac 1 2$, where \[ L=\int_0^T\int_0^t|\widehat{c}(t,s)|^2dsdt, \quad K_1=\int_0^T\int_0^t|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^2dsdt,\quad K_2=\int_0^T\int_0^t|P_0(t,s)|^2dsdt, \] $P_0$ is defined in (\ref{6.3}) with $A=\widehat{f}$. nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: Given $y(\cdot )\in L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\dbR),$ consider the following Volterra equation \begin{eqnarray} x(t)=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}A(t,s)x(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}B(t,r)B(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}y(s)drds, \end{eqnarray} which obviously admits a unique solution $x(\cdot)$ under above assumptions. By using Lemma 1.1 in \cite{Y 1996}, we can rewrite (\ref{6.5}) as \[ x(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t} \widehat{B}(t,r)B(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}y(s)drds. \] Then using the idea of contraction mapping and Lemma \ref{lemma-1}, together with above requirements, we can obtain the existence of $x(\cdot)$ in $L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\dbR)$ satisfying (\ref{6.4}).
nodes.statement_short: Freeze $y$, solve the resulting Volterra equation, remove the Volterra drift by the resolvent, and close the argument by contraction mapping with Lemma 3.1.

nodes.name: freeze $y$ and solve the auxiliary Volterra equation
nodes.statement: Given $y(\cdot )\in L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\dbR),$ consider the following Volterra equation \begin{eqnarray} x(t)=\varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}A(t,s)x(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t}B(t,r)B(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}y(s)drds, \end{eqnarray} which obviously admits a unique solution $x(\cdot)$ under above assumptions.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the fixed-point map by freezing the double-integral term at a given $y$.

nodes.name: remove the Volterra drift with the resolvent
nodes.statement: By using Lemma 1.1 in \cite{Y 1996}, we can rewrite (\ref{6.5}) as \[ x(t)=\widehat{\varphi }(t)-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{s\wedge t} \widehat{B}(t,r)B(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{r}}y(s)drds. \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply the variation-of-constants formula so only the double integral remains.

nodes.name: conclude by contraction mapping
nodes.statement: Then using the idea of contraction mapping and Lemma \ref{lemma-1}, together with above requirements, we can obtain the existence of $x(\cdot)$ in $L_{\mathcal{F}}^{2}(0,T;\dbR)$ satisfying (\ref{6.4}).
nodes.statement_short: Contraction mapping plus Lemma 3.1 give existence and the $L^2$ estimate.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: From (\ref{3.14}) and (\ref{3.20}), we know the difference between $\overline{x}_i$ and $\widehat{a}$ satisfies the type of Equation (\ref{6.1}) with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$, $\varphi=\widehat{\sigma}_i$. Then by means of (\ref{6.4}), \begin{eqnarray*} \dbE\int_0^T|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt &\leq &C\dbE\int_0^T\left\vert \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t)\right\vert ^{2}dt. \end{eqnarray*} It then follows from the boundedness of $\sigma$ and $P$ in (\ref{3.8.1}), together with the independence of $W_i$ ($i=1,2,\cdots,N$) that \[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt=O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right), \] which implies the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Identify $\overline{x}_i-\widehat{a}$ as a solution of (6.1) with forcing $\widehat{\sigma}_i$, then use independence of the $W_i$ to get the $O(1/N)$ averaging gain.

nodes.name: identify the difference equation
nodes.statement: From (\ref{3.14}) and (\ref{3.20}), we know the difference between $\overline{x}_i$ and $\widehat{a}$ satisfies the type of Equation (\ref{6.1}) with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$, $\varphi=\widehat{\sigma}_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Recognize $\overline{x}_i-\widehat{a}$ as an instance of the abstract equation (6.1).

nodes.name: apply the a priori estimate (6.4)
nodes.statement: Then by means of (\ref{6.4}), \begin{eqnarray*} \dbE\int_0^T|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt &\leq &C\dbE\int_0^T\left\vert \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t)\right\vert ^{2}dt. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the averaged deviation by the averaged noise term using Lemma 3.2.

nodes.name: exploit independence of the Brownian motions
nodes.statement: It then follows from the boundedness of $\sigma$ and $P$ in (\ref{3.8.1}), together with the independence of $W_i$ ($i=1,2,\cdots,N$) that \[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt=O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right), \] which implies the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Independence makes the averaged noise of order $1/N$, giving the claim.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.4
nodes.statement: Comparing (\ref{3.19}) and (\ref{3.20}), we can rewrite $x_i(t)$ as \begin{align*} x_i(t)=& \; \overline{x}_i(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds \\ &-\frac{1}{R}\int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x_i(s)-\overline{x}_i(s)]drds. \end{align*} Therefore, \begin{align*} x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)=& \; \overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds\nonumber\\ & - \frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds\nonumber\\ &+\frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_r}[\overline{x}^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds. \end{align*} By using Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, Lemma \ref{lemma-2}, together with the boundedness of $\widehat{f}$ and $\widehat{c}$, we can obtain the desired result (\ref{3.23}).
nodes.statement_short: Subtract the limiting state equation from the realized one, average over $i$, and apply Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3.

nodes.name: rewrite $x_i$ around the limiting state
nodes.statement: Comparing (\ref{3.19}) and (\ref{3.20}), we can rewrite $x_i(t)$ as \begin{align*} x_i(t)=& \; \overline{x}_i(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds \\ &-\frac{1}{R}\int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x_i(s)-\overline{x}_i(s)]drds. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Express the realized state as the limiting state plus deviation terms.

nodes.name: average over the population
nodes.statement: Therefore, \begin{align*} x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)=& \; \overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)+\int_0^t\widehat{f}(t,s)\Big[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)\Big]ds\nonumber\\ & - \frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_r}[x^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds\nonumber\\ &+\frac 1 R \int_0^T\int_0^{s\wedge t}\widehat{c}(t,r)\widehat{c}(s,r)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_r}[\overline{x}^N(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]drds. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Derive the closed equation satisfied by $x^{N}-\widehat{a}$.

nodes.name: apply Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3
nodes.statement: By using Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, Lemma \ref{lemma-2}, together with the boundedness of $\widehat{f}$ and $\widehat{c}$, we can obtain the desired result (\ref{3.23}).
nodes.statement_short: Combine the well-posedness estimate with the $O(1/N)$ bound of Lemma 3.3.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement: First from the definition of $\mathcal{J}_i$ in (\ref{2.2}) and $\overline{J}_i$ in (\ref{3.2}), \begin{align*} \mathcal{J}_{i}(\widehat{u}_{i},\widehat{u}_{-i})-\overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i}) \leq & \; C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert R|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}-R|\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}\right\vert dt \\ &+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert |x_{i}(t)-\gamma x^{N}(t)-\eta |^{2}-|\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |^{2}\right\vert dt \\ \leq & \; C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}R\left[ |\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}+2|\overline{u}_{i}(t)|\cdot|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|\right] dt \\ &+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|^{2}dt \\ &+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |\cdot |x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|dt, \end{align*} where $x_{i}$ and $\overline{x}_{i}$ satisfy (\ref{3.19}) and (\ref{3.20}) respectively. It follows from (\ref{3.3}) and (\ref{3.18}) that \begin{align*} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt \leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\left\vert \int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(s,t)[x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)]ds\right\vert ^{2}dt \\ \leq & \; C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds. \end{align*} Note that equation (\ref{3.20}) is one special case of (\ref{6.1}) with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Under above requirement, then from inequality (\ref{6.4}) above we have the boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\dbR)$. Recalling (\ref{3.6}) with $a=\widehat{a}$, we can also get similar boundedness result for $\overline{u}_i$. As a result, by Schwarz's inequality, \begin{align*} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{u}_{i}(t)||\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|dt \leq & \left[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}} \left[\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}} \\ \leq & \; C\left[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*} On the other hand, \begin{eqnarray*} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|^{2}dt \leq C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt. \end{eqnarray*} Similarly, we can use Schwarz's inequality to estimate \begin{eqnarray*} &&\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |\cdot |x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{(N)}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|dt\\ &&\leq C\left[\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right]^{\frac 1 2}+C\left[\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\right]^{\frac 1 2}. \end{eqnarray*} Therefore, by using Lemma \ref{lemma-3}, we obtain the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the cost difference into control and state deviation terms, bound each by Schwarz's inequality, and insert the $O(1/N)$ rate of Lemma 3.4.

nodes.name: expand the cost difference
nodes.statement: First from the definition of $\mathcal{J}_i$ in (\ref{2.2}) and $\overline{J}_i$ in (\ref{3.2}), \begin{align*} \mathcal{J}_{i}(\widehat{u}_{i},\widehat{u}_{-i})-\overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i}) \leq & \; C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert R|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}-R|\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}\right\vert dt \\ &+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert |x_{i}(t)-\gamma x^{N}(t)-\eta |^{2}-|\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |^{2}\right\vert dt \\ \leq & \; C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}R\left[ |\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}+2|\overline{u}_{i}(t)|\cdot|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|\right] dt \\ &+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|^{2}dt \\ &+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |\cdot |x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|dt, \end{align*} where $x_{i}$ and $\overline{x}_{i}$ satisfy (\ref{3.19}) and (\ref{3.20}) respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Split the cost gap into a control-deviation part and two state-deviation parts.

nodes.name: bound the control deviation
nodes.statement: It follows from (\ref{3.3}) and (\ref{3.18}) that \begin{align*} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt \leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\left\vert \int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(s,t)[x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)]ds\right\vert ^{2}dt \\ \leq & \; C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Control deviation is controlled by state deviation through the kernel $\widehat{c}$.

nodes.name: boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$, $\overline{u}_i$ and the cross term
nodes.statement: Note that equation (\ref{3.20}) is one special case of (\ref{6.1}) with $A=0,$ $B=\widehat{c}$. Under above requirement, then from inequality (\ref{6.4}) above we have the boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\dbR)$. Recalling (\ref{3.6}) with $a=\widehat{a}$, we can also get similar boundedness result for $\overline{u}_i$. As a result, by Schwarz's inequality, \begin{align*} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{u}_{i}(t)||\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|dt \leq & \left[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}} \left[\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)-\overline{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}} \\ \leq & \; C\left[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)-\overline{x}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\right] ^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Lemma 3.2 for boundedness, then Schwarz's inequality on the cross term.

nodes.name: bound the remaining state-deviation terms
nodes.statement: On the other hand, \begin{eqnarray*} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|^{2}dt \leq C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt. \end{eqnarray*} Similarly, we can use Schwarz's inequality to estimate \begin{eqnarray*} &&\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |\cdot |x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma (x^{(N)}(t)-\widehat{a}(t))|dt\\ &&\leq C\left[\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\overline{x}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\right]^{\frac 1 2}+C\left[\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\right]^{\frac 1 2}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce both state terms to $\|x_i-\overline{x}_i\|$ and $\|x^{N}-\widehat{a}\|$.

nodes.name: conclude via Lemma 3.4
nodes.statement: Therefore, by using Lemma \ref{lemma-3}, we obtain the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Insert the $O(1/N)$ estimates of Lemma 3.4 to reach the $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ rate.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: For convenience, we can rewrite (\ref{6.7}) as \begin{align*} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}^{\prime }(s)ds \\ &+\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s). \end{align*} Here $u_{i}^{\prime }(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s),$ \[ \overline{u}_{i}(s)=-\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr, \] where $x_{i}$ satisfies (\ref{6.7}), $\widehat{c}$ is given in (\ref{3.7}). It then follows from inequality (\ref{6.8}) that $\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$. Next we construct one auxiliary optimal control problem with state equation and cost functional as \begin{align} \widetilde{x}_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)\widetilde{x}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\ &+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}''(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s,\widetilde{x}_{i})ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align} and \[ \widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')=\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left[|\widetilde{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |^{2}+R|u_{i}''(t)+\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})|^{2}\right]dt. \] where $u''_{i}$ is the control variable. For $t\in[0,T]$, $\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})$ in (\ref{6.9}) is defined as \[ \overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})=-\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[\widetilde{x}_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr. \] Obviously, $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')$ attains its minimum when $u_{i}''=0,$ and the corresponding cost functional equals to $\overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i}).$ On the other hand, by Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, \[ M_{i}'(t)=\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)M_{i}'(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)M_{i}'(r)drds \] admits a unique solution $M_{i}'$ such that \[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|M_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C. \] If we take $u_{i}''=u_{i}'(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s)$, and $\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ is the corresponding solution of (\ref{6.9}), then $\widetilde{x}_{i}'=\overline{x}_{i}(t)+M_{i}'(t),$ where $\overline{x}_{i}(t)$ is the optimal state in (\ref{3.9}) with $a=\widehat{a}$. Moreover, recalling the boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\dbR)$, we also have $\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widetilde{x}_{i}'(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$. Since $x_{i}$ and $\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ are given in (\ref{6.7}) and (\ref{6.9}), thus their difference $d_{i}=x_{i}-\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ satisfy \[ d_{i}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)d_{i}(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)d_{i}(r)drds. \] Under above requirements, from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, we have \[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\widetilde{x}_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C\epsilon _{a}^{2}. \] Following the similar arguments in \cite{N-H 2012}, we should have \[ |J_{i}^{\xi}(u_{i})-\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')| \leq C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon _{a}+\epsilon _{b}), \] where $C$ does not depend on $\xi_a$ and $\xi_b$. After combining the estimate of $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')\geq \overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)$, we can get the desired result.

nodes.statement: For convenience, we can rewrite (\ref{6.7}) as \begin{align*} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}^{\prime }(s)ds \\ &+\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s). \end{align*} Here $u_{i}^{\prime }(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s),$ \[ \overline{u}_{i}(s)=-\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr, \] where $x_{i}$ satisfies (\ref{6.7}), $\widehat{c}$ is given in (\ref{3.7}).

nodes.name: construct the auxiliary control problem
nodes.statement: Next we construct one auxiliary optimal control problem with state equation and cost functional as \begin{align} \widetilde{x}_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi (t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)\widetilde{x}_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\ &+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}''(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\overline{u}_{i}(s,\widetilde{x}_{i})ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma (t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align} and \[ \widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')=\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left[|\widetilde{x}_{i}(t)-\gamma \widehat{a}(t)-\eta |^{2}+R|u_{i}''(t)+\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})|^{2}\right]dt. \] where $u''_{i}$ is the control variable. For $t\in[0,T]$, $\overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})$ in (\ref{6.9}) is defined as \[ \overline{u}_{i}(t,\widetilde{x}_{i})=-\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[\widetilde{x}_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr. \]

nodes.name: minimum of the auxiliary cost
nodes.statement: Obviously, $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}'')$ attains its minimum when $u_{i}''=0,$ and the corresponding cost functional equals to $\overline{J}_{i}(\overline{u}_{i}).$

nodes.name: solve for the correction $M_i'$ by Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, \[ M_{i}'(t)=\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)M_{i}'(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)M_{i}'(r)drds \] admits a unique solution $M_{i}'$ such that \[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|M_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}'(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C. \]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 gives a unique bounded correction process $M_i'$.

nodes.name: identify $\widetilde{x}_i'=\overline{x}_i+M_i'$
nodes.statement: If we take $u_{i}''=u_{i}'(s)=u_{i}(s)-\overline{u}_{i}(s)$, and $\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ is the corresponding solution of (\ref{6.9}), then $\widetilde{x}_{i}'=\overline{x}_{i}(t)+M_{i}'(t),$ where $\overline{x}_{i}(t)$ is the optimal state in (\ref{3.9}) with $a=\widehat{a}$. Moreover, recalling the boundedness of $\overline{x}_i$ in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\dbR)$, we also have $\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widetilde{x}_{i}'(t)|^{2}dt\leq C$.
nodes.statement_short: Choosing $u_i''=u_i'$ decomposes the auxiliary state into the optimal state plus $M_i'$.

nodes.name: estimate the difference $d_i=x_i-\widetilde{x}_i'$
nodes.statement: Since $x_{i}$ and $\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ are given in (\ref{6.7}) and (\ref{6.9}), thus their difference $d_{i}=x_{i}-\widetilde{x}_{i}'$ satisfy \[ d_{i}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)d_{i}(s)ds-\frac{1}{R}\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)\dbE^{\mathcal{F}_{t}}\!\!\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)d_{i}(r)drds. \] Under above requirements, from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1}, we have \[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)-\widetilde{x}_{i}^{\prime }(t)|^{2}dt\leq 6\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{0}^{t}g(t,s)\xi _{a}(s)ds\right\vert^{2}dt\leq C\epsilon _{a}^{2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: The state gap between perturbed and auxiliary problems is $O(\epsilon_a)$ in $L^2$.

nodes.name: compare the cost functionals and conclude
nodes.statement: Following the similar arguments in \cite{N-H 2012}, we should have \[ |J_{i}^{\xi}(u_{i})-\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')| \leq C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon _{a}+\epsilon _{b}), \] where $C$ does not depend on $\xi_a$ and $\xi_b$. After combining the estimate of $\widetilde{J}_{i}(u_{i}')\geq \overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)$, we can get the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: The cost gap is $C(1+\epsilon_b)(\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b)$, which yields the claimed lower bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement: If we can prove \[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C,\quad \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C, \] where $x_i$ satisfies (\ref{3.19}), $C$ does not depend on $N,$ then the result holds directly. From (\ref{3.19}), we have \begin{align} x^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \nonumber \\ &-\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}s}\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds, \end{align} where $x^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{l=1}^{N}x_{l}(t).$ Note that (\ref{6.10}) is one special case of equation (\ref{6.1}), (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1} that \begin{align} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(s)|^{2}ds \leq & \; C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi}(s)|^{2}ds+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert \frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma}_{l}(t)\right\vert ^{2}dt \nonumber \\ & +C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds+C. \end{align} As to $x_i$ in equation (\ref{3.19}), using (\ref{6.11}) and conditions (\ref{6.2}), (\ref{6.3}) with $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, we should have $\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C$ where $C$ is independent of $N$. At last, we know that \begin{align*} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt = & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr\right\vert ^{2}dt \\ \leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{t}^{T}|\widehat{c}(r,t)|^{2}drdt\cdot \dbE\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]^{2}dr. \end{align*} Hence $\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$ is bounded, too. Then the desired result holds.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $L^2$ bounds on $x_i$ and $\widehat{u}_i$, which follow from applying Lemma 3.2 to the equation satisfied by the population average.

nodes.name: reduce to two $L^2$ bounds
nodes.statement: If we can prove \[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C,\quad \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C, \] where $x_i$ satisfies (\ref{3.19}), $C$ does not depend on $N,$ then the result holds directly.

nodes.name: equation for the population average
nodes.statement: From (\ref{3.19}), we have \begin{align} x^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)x^{N}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \nonumber \\ &-\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}s}\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds, \end{align} where $x^{N}(t)=\frac{1}{N}\sum\limits_{l=1}^{N}x_{l}(t).$

nodes.name: apply Lemma 3.2 to the averaged equation
nodes.statement: Note that (\ref{6.10}) is one special case of equation (\ref{6.1}), (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold for $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6-1} that \begin{align} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(s)|^{2}ds \leq & \; C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi}(s)|^{2}ds+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert \frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma}_{l}(t)\right\vert ^{2}dt \nonumber \\ & +C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds+C. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 bounds the $L^2$ norm of the population average.

nodes.name: bound the individual state
nodes.statement: As to $x_i$ in equation (\ref{3.19}), using (\ref{6.11}) and conditions (\ref{6.2}), (\ref{6.3}) with $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, we should have $\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(s)|^{2}ds\leq C$ where $C$ is independent of $N$.

nodes.name: bound the control and conclude
nodes.statement: At last, we know that \begin{align*} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt = & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr\right\vert ^{2}dt \\ \leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\int_{0}^{T}\int_{t}^{T}|\widehat{c}(r,t)|^{2}drdt\cdot \dbE\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(r)-\gamma\widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]^{2}dr. \end{align*} Hence $\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$ is bounded, too. Then the desired result holds.
nodes.statement_short: The control bound follows from the state bound, giving boundedness of the cost.

nodes.name: compute the population average
nodes.statement: After some direct calculations, \begin{align*} x^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \\ & -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}s}\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[x^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds \\ & +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds+\frac{1}{N}\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]ds, \end{align*} where $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{f}$, $\widehat{\sigma}_l$ are defined in (\ref{3.8.1}).
nodes.statement_short: The single deviation enters the average only through a $1/N$ factor.

nodes.name: compute the limiting average via Fubini
nodes.statement: Using Fubini theorem, it also follows from (\ref{3.9}) (with $a=\widehat{a}$) that \begin{align*} \overline{x}^{N}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{l=1}^{N}\widehat{\sigma }_{l}(t) \\ & -\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)\frac{1}{R}\dbE^{\mathcal{F}s}\!\!\int_{s}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,s)[\overline{x}^{N}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]drds, \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Obtain the corresponding equation for the limiting average $\overline{x}^{N}$.

nodes.statement_short: Subtracting gives a closed equation of type (6.1) for the mean-field error.

nodes.name: apply Lemma 3.2 to obtain (6.17)
nodes.statement: Note that if $A=0$, $B=\widehat{c}$, then (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) imply $\overline{x}^N$ is bounded in $L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(0,T;\dbR).$ Similarly, if (\ref{6.2}) and (\ref{6.3}) hold with  $A=\widehat{f}$, $B=\widehat{c}$, then using Lemma \ref{lemma6-1} to (\ref{6.16}), we have \begin{eqnarray} &&\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt \nonumber\\ &&\leq (1+K_2)\left[(36+12R^2)\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt+\frac{36}{N^{2}}L\cdot \dbE\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds\right], \end{eqnarray} where $L$ and $K_2$ are defined before.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 converts the error equation into a quantitative $L^2$ bound.

nodes.name: bound the deviation using Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from Lemma \ref{lemma6.3}, $\mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$ is bounded, it then suffices to consider $u_i$ in (\ref{6.13}) such that $\mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\leq \mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})$, which implies that $\dbE\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C$.  As to $\widehat{u}_i$ in (\ref{6.15}), we have \begin{align*} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt = & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left\vert\int_{t}^{T}\widehat{c}(r,t)[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]dr\right\vert ^{2}dt \\ \leq & \; \frac{1}{R^{2}}L\cdot \dbE\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(r)-\gamma \widehat{a}(r)-\eta ]^{2}dr, \end{align*} therefore, \begin{align} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds \leq & \; 2\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(s)|^{2}ds+2\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{u}_{i}(s)|^{2}ds \nonumber \\ \leq & \; C+\frac{2}{R^{2}}L\cdot \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(r)|^{2}dr, \end{align} where $C$ does not depend on $N$.
nodes.statement_short: Only deviations that do not worsen the cost matter, so $u_i$ is $L^2$ bounded.

nodes.name: substitute (6.18) into (6.17)
nodes.statement: Substituting (\ref{6.18}) into (\ref{6.17}), we have \begin{eqnarray} &&\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\nonumber\\ && \leq (1+K_2)(36+12R^2)\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt\nonumber \\ &&+\frac{C}{N^{2}}+ (1+K_2)\frac{72}{N^{2}R^2}L^2\cdot \dbE\int_{0}^{T}[u_{i}(s)-\widehat{u}_{i}(s)]^{2}ds. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Combine the two estimates into a single inequality for the mean-field error.

nodes.name: estimate the individual state
nodes.statement: After some transformations, we can rewrite (\ref{6.13}) as \begin{align*} x_{i}(t) = & \; \widehat{\varphi }(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)[x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)]ds \\ & +\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{f}(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\widehat{c}(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\widehat{\sigma }_{i}(t), \end{align*} therefore, \begin{align} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt \leq & \; 5\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\varphi }(t)|^{2}dt+5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^{2}dsdt\cdot\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x^{N}(s)-\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds \nonumber \\ & +5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{f}(t,s)|^2dsdt\cdot \int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{a}(s)|^{2}ds \nonumber \\ & +5\int_{0}^{T}\int_{0}^{t}|\widehat{c}(t,s)|^{2}dsdt\cdot\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|u_{i}(s)|^{2}ds+\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\widehat{\sigma}_{i}(t)|^{2}dt. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|x_i\|_{L^2}$ by the mean-field error plus bounded terms.

nodes.name: absorb the $x_i$ term and conclude
nodes.statement: Since $\widehat{\varphi}$, $\widehat{f}$, $\widehat{a}$, $\sigma$ are bounded, substituting (\ref{6.19}) into (\ref{6.20}) yields \begin{eqnarray*} \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt+ (1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2\cdot \dbE\int_{0}^{T}[x_{i}(s)]^{2}ds. \end{eqnarray*} So if $(1+K_2)K_1\frac{360}{N^{2}R^2}L^2<\frac 1 2,$ then we have \[ \dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt\leq C+C\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|\overline{x}^{N}(t)-\widehat{a}(t)|^{2}dt, \] which implies the boundedness of $\dbE\int_{0}^{T}|x_{i}(t)|^{2}dt$. By combining (\ref{6.19}), (\ref{6.20}) and Lemma \ref{lemma-2}, we obtained the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: The smallness condition lets the $x_i$ term be absorbed, and Lemma 3.3 supplies the $O(1/N)$ rate.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.4
nodes.statement: If we denote by $\xi_a(t)=x^N(t)-\widehat{a}(t),$ $\xi_b(t)=\gamma(\widehat{a}(t)-x^N(t))$, then the dynamics and cost functional of $\mathcal{A}_i$ can be rewritten as \begin{align} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\ & +\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\xi_{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align} and \[ J_{i}(u_{i})=\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left[ |x_{i}(t)-\gamma\widehat{a}(t)-\eta +\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\right]dt. \] From Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, we have $\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b=O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}})$, and $\dbE\int_0^T|x_i(t)|^2dt+\dbE\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C,$ where $C$ is independent of $N$, $\epsilon_a$, $\epsilon_b$ are defined in (\ref{6.6}), it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, Theorem \ref{theorem3.2} that \[ \mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\geq \overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right) \geq \mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right). \] The conclusion is thus proved.
nodes.statement_short: Recast the $N$-player game as a perturbed limiting problem with $\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b=O(1/\sqrt{N})$, then chain Lemma 3.7 with Theorem 3.3.

nodes.name: identify the perturbations $\xi_a$, $\xi_b$
nodes.statement: If we denote by $\xi_a(t)=x^N(t)-\widehat{a}(t),$ $\xi_b(t)=\gamma(\widehat{a}(t)-x^N(t))$, then the dynamics and cost functional of $\mathcal{A}_i$ can be rewritten as \begin{align} x_{i}(t) = & \; \varphi(t)+\int_{0}^{t}b(t,s)x_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\widehat{a}(s)ds \nonumber \\ & +\int_{0}^{t}f(t,s)\xi_{a}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}c(t,s)u_{i}(s)ds+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t,s)dW_{i}(s), \end{align} and \[ J_{i}(u_{i})=\dbE\int_{0}^{T}\left[ |x_{i}(t)-\gamma\widehat{a}(t)-\eta +\xi _{b}(t)|^{2}+R|u_{i}(t)|^{2}\right]dt. \]
nodes.statement_short: Write the true game as the perturbed limiting problem with explicit $\xi_a$, $\xi_b$.

nodes.name: apply Lemma 3.7 and Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement: From Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, we have $\epsilon_a+\epsilon_b=O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}})$, and $\dbE\int_0^T|x_i(t)|^2dt+\dbE\int_0^T|u_i(t)|^2dt\leq C,$ where $C$ is independent of $N$, $\epsilon_a$, $\epsilon_b$ are defined in (\ref{6.6}), it then follows from Lemma \ref{lemma6.4}, Theorem \ref{theorem3.2} that \[ \mathcal{J}_i(u_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})\geq \overline{J}_i(\overline{u}_i)-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right) \geq \mathcal{J}_i(\widehat{u}_i,\widehat{u}_{-i})-O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\right). \]
nodes.statement_short: Chain the perturbation bound with the cost approximation to get the $\epsilon$-Nash inequality.
